slowdown.note: No call to slow frontier AI; her FRONTIER Act release says it protects against catastrophic risks 'without slowing the innovation', which frames the bill but is not a stated position against a safety slowdown.

pause.note: She describes her FRONTIER Act (sponsor) as including 'a government pause button if a model poses an imminent risk of catastrophe', an emergency stop for a specific dangerous model rather than a general halt to frontier development; reviewer may prefer 'none'.

intl.note: No statement found on coordinating with China on AI pacing.

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI.

record: Lead sponsor, with Rep. Jay Obernolte, of the FRONTIER Act: tiered transparency, independent audits, incident reporting and emergency authority over the most advanced AI models, aimed at catastrophic risk.
Co-released with Rep. Obernolte the discussion draft of the Great American AI Act, a federal AI framework that would also limit state AI development rules for three years.
Co-led with Rep. Don Beyer a 10-member bipartisan letter urging House leaders to act immediately on AI legislation 'before true catastrophes occur'.
Released the CLAIM Act discussion draft on liability of AI developers for harms caused by their AI agents.
grade_reason: In 2026 she said in her own words that frontier labs' models 'could actually cause a catastrophe' and that her bill protects the public from 'catastrophic risks', without limiting this to misuse. Both are general and flagged boundary, so B versus C is a judgment call; no dismissive statement was found.
